project.name: nisshi
project.description: Stateless, Apache Kafka-compatible broker written in Rust with pluggable storage backends (PostgreSQL, libSQL/SQLite, S3/object store, memory); schema-backed topics can be written as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake tables.

nodes.languageNotes: Roughly 80 near-identical fixture tests (raw bytes -> decode -> assert struct fields); represented at the file level rather than as individual nodes since each covers one API/version combination in a mechanical, repetitive pattern.

nodes.name: describe_configs.rs
nodes.summary: Round-trip test for the DescribeConfigsResponse wire format, validating nested resource/config-entry encoding against a captured payload.

nodes.name: describe_topic_partitions.rs
nodes.summary: Round-trip test for the DescribeTopicPartitionsRequest wire format used by topic/partition metadata discovery.

nodes.name: encode.rs
nodes.summary: Extensive suite of encode-only round-trip tests mirroring decode.rs, validating that in-memory Kafka message structs serialize back to the exact captured wire bytes for each API/version.
nodes.languageNotes: Roughly 45 near-identical fixture tests (struct -> encode -> assert bytes); represented at the file level rather than as individual nodes since each covers one API/version combination in a mechanical, repetitive pattern.

nodes.name: fetch.rs
nodes.summary: Round-trip test for FetchRequest wire-format encoding/decoding against a captured multi-partition fetch payload.

nodes.name: fetch_response.rs
nodes.summary: Field-by-field round-trip tests for FetchResponse, covering throttle time, per-partition error codes, high watermark, diverging epoch, snapshot id, and node endpoints.

nodes.name: find_coordinator.rs
nodes.summary: Round-trip test for FindCoordinatorRequest/Response wire format used in group and transaction coordinator discovery.

nodes.name: gap6.rs
nodes.summary: Negative/robustness test suite ("Gap 6") asserting the decoder returns Err rather than panicking on malformed, truncated, oversized, or otherwise invalid frame bytes.
nodes.languageNotes: Organized as a systematic matrix of edge cases (empty input, truncation at each header field, unknown/negative API keys, corrupt lengths, oversized size fields) intended to harden the decoder against malformed or adversarial input.

nodes.name: snappy.rs
nodes.summary: Integration tests decompressing and decoding Snappy-compressed Kafka record batches at increasing scale (100, 500, and 1,000 records) captured from a real producer.
nodes.languageNotes: Test fixtures embed raw captured Snappy-compressed byte payloads directly as literals, so file size scales with fixture size rather than logic complexity.

nodes.name: version.rs
nodes.summary: Round-trip tests for JoinGroupResponse and OffsetFetchResponse verifying header/body encoding stays correct across supported API versions.

nodes.name: check_message_meta
nodes.summary: Builds an expected byte payload for AddPartitionsToTxn, decodes it into a Frame, and asserts the decoded request/response round-trips back to the same bytes.

nodes.name: produce_request
nodes.summary: Constructs a ProduceRequest containing a record batch and asserts its encoded bytes match a captured reference payload, parameterized by compression codec.

nodes.name: as_records
nodes.summary: Test helper that decodes a raw record-batch byte slice into an inflated record batch for use as fixture data.

nodes.name: init_tracing
nodes.summary: Installs a scoped tracing subscriber that logs to a per-test-thread file under logs/<crate>/, returning a guard that resets the default subscriber on drop.

nodes.name: initial_state
nodes.summary: Verifies a newly built GroupConsumer starts in the outsider state with its configured group id and topic list.

nodes.name: outsider_sends_join_request

nodes.name: outsider_member_id_required_rejoins_with_assigned_id
nodes.summary: Verifies that when the broker rejects a join with MemberIdRequired, the consumer retries JoinGroup using the broker-assigned member id.

nodes.name: outsider_becomes_follower
nodes.summary: Verifies a consumer that is not selected as group leader transitions to the follower role after a JoinGroupResponse.

nodes.name: outsider_becomes_leader_range
nodes.summary: Verifies a consumer selected as group leader computes and emits a SyncGroupRequest with Range-assignor partition assignments for all group members.

nodes.name: leader_uses_protocol_from_join_response
nodes.summary: Verifies the elected leader honors the protocol name chosen by the broker in the JoinGroupResponse when computing member assignments.

nodes.name: leader_sync_response_yields_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Verifies that after the leader receives its own SyncGroupResponse, the consumer's next action is a HeartbeatRequest.

nodes.name: follower_heartbeat_ok_yields_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Verifies a follower consumer continues emitting HeartbeatRequests while the group state remains stable.

nodes.name: follower_rebalance_in_progress_yields_join
nodes.summary: Verifies a follower receiving a RebalanceInProgress heartbeat error rejoins the group via a new JoinGroupRequest.

nodes.name: member_meta

nodes.summary: Builds an expected multi-topic CreateTopicsRequest/Response byte payload and asserts decode/encode round-trips exactly.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Core of the nisshi-storage crate: defines the Storage trait and its Kafka domain types (Topition, MetadataResponse, GroupDetail, transaction and SCRAM types, Error), plus the StorageContainer enum and Builder that select and dispatch to a concrete backend at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: StorageContainer is a runtime-selected enum-of-backends dispatch pattern: Builder::build() picks a backend from a URL scheme, and every Storage method on StorageContainer simply forwards to the active variant.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Crate-wide error enum aggregating I/O, protocol, SQL, object-store, schema, and pool errors from every storage backend, with `From` conversions from each underlying error type.

nodes.name: Topition
nodes.summary: Identifies a Kafka topic-partition pair; the primary key used throughout the storage layer to address produce/fetch/offset operations.

nodes.name: TopitionOffset
nodes.summary: Pairs a topic-partition with a specific offset.

nodes.name: ListOffsetResponse
nodes.summary: Result of a ListOffsets query: the resolved offset, its timestamp, and an error code.

nodes.name: OffsetCommitRequest

nodes.name: TopicId
nodes.summary: Identifies a topic by name or generated id, with conversions to/from the wire-protocol topic identifiers.

nodes.name: BrokerRegistrationRequest

nodes.name: MetadataResponse

nodes.name: OffsetStage
nodes.summary: Log-start, high-watermark, and last-stable offsets for a topic-partition at a point in time.

nodes.name: GroupMember

nodes.name: GroupState
nodes.summary: Protocol type/name, leader, and member assignments for a consumer group in the Forming or Formed state.

nodes.name: ConsumerGroupState

nodes.name: GroupDetail

nodes.name: GroupDetailResponse

nodes.name: NamedGroupDetail

nodes.name: PartitionDetail

nodes.name: Version

nodes.name: ProducerIdResponse

nodes.name: TxnState

nodes.summary: Generic layer that pairs an inner service with an expected typed Kafka request marker, used to compose per-request-type service stacks.

nodes.name: RequestService
nodes.summary: Generic service that converts an inbound Frame body into a typed Kafka request via TryFrom, delegates to the inner service, and converts the typed response back into a frame body.

nodes.name: RequestService::serve
nodes.summary: Delegates a typed request to the inner service and logs the outcome, returning the raw response.

nodes.name: FrameRequestLayer
nodes.summary: Frame-level counterpart of RequestLayer, pairing an inner service with a typed request marker for frame-oriented dispatch.

nodes.name: FrameRequestService
nodes.summary: Service that extracts a typed request from an incoming Frame, invokes the inner service, and packages the typed response back into a response Frame.

nodes.name: FrameRequestService::serve
nodes.summary: Extracts the typed request from an incoming frame body via TryFrom, invokes the inner service, and maps the result back onto the response frame body.

nodes.name: BytesFrameLayer
nodes.summary: Top-level rama Layer configuring optional SASL authentication and producing the BytesFrameService that turns raw bytes into parsed Kafka frames.

nodes.name: BytesFrameLayer::layer
nodes.summary: Builds a BytesFrameService by constructing a server-side Authentication state machine from the configured SASL config, wrapped for shared mutable access.

nodes.name: AuthenticationFrame
nodes.summary: Per-connection authentication state combining the rama Authentication handshake driver with a mutex-guarded SASL protocol version, tracking whether the connection has completed authentication.

nodes.name: BytesFrameService
nodes.summary: Service that parses raw bytes into a Kafka Frame, enforces SASL authentication gating on protected API keys, drives the SASL handshake state machine, and records API request/error metrics before delegating to the inner service.

nodes.name: BytesFrameService::serve
nodes.summary: Core connection-handling entry point: parses raw bytes into a request frame off the async runtime, enforces SASL authentication before allowing protected API keys through, drives the SASL handshake (challenge/response) when unauthenticated, tracks per-request metrics and progress reporting, and serializes the inner service's response back to bytes.

nodes.name: FrameBytesLayer
nodes.summary: Thin pass-through layer producing FrameBytesService, the counterpart to BytesFrameLayer that serializes a response Frame back to bytes.

nodes.name: FrameBytesService
nodes.summary: Service that serializes an outgoing typed request into a Frame, sends it through the inner service, and parses the raw response bytes back into a Frame.

nodes.name: FrameBytesService::serve
nodes.summary: Builds a request Frame from the typed request, sends it through the inner service, and parses the raw response bytes back into a Frame using the negotiated API key/version.

nodes.name: FrameBodyLayer
nodes.summary: Pass-through layer producing FrameBodyService, which extracts a frame's message body for inner services that operate on bodies rather than whole frames.

nodes.name: FrameBodyService
nodes.summary: Service that unwraps a Frame into its message body, delegates to the inner body-oriented service, and re-wraps the result into a response frame.

nodes.name: FrameBodyService::serve
nodes.summary: Extracts the message body from an incoming frame, forwards it to the inner service, and wraps the resulting body back into a response frame.

nodes.name: BodyRequestLayer
nodes.summary: Layer pairing an inner service with a typed request marker at the message-body level, used when composing body-oriented request handlers.

nodes.name: BodyRequestService
nodes.summary: Service that converts a message body into a typed Kafka request, invokes the inner service, and converts the typed response back into a body.

nodes.name: RequestFrameLayer
nodes.summary: Layer producing RequestFrameService, the client-side counterpart that turns a typed outgoing request into a Frame and turns the response frame back into a typed response.

nodes.name: RequestFrameService
nodes.summary: Client-facing service that builds a request Frame from a typed request, sends it through the inner service, and converts the response frame back into the typed response.

nodes.name: RequestFrameService::serve
nodes.summary: Builds a request frame for the typed outgoing request with a resolved API version, sends it through the inner service, and converts the raw response body back into the typed response.

nodes.name: FrameService
nodes.summary: Trivial service that always returns a pre-configured static response for any incoming frame, useful for stubbing or testing a route.

nodes.name: ResponseService
nodes.summary: Trivial service that always returns a pre-configured static typed response, the typed-request counterpart of FrameService used for stubbing routes.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-service re-exporting the api/channel/consumer/frame/stream submodules; defines the crate-wide Error type, DNS/host-port resolution helpers instrumented with OpenTelemetry metrics, and a LatencyIntroducingLayer for injecting artificial latency into the service stack.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Crate-wide error enum covering auth, routing, framing, I/O, join, message, channel, mutex-poison, parse, protocol, and DNS-resolution failure cases, each convertible via From impls.

nodes.name: LatencyIntroducingLayer
nodes.summary: Rama Layer configuring a seeded RNG and a millisecond latency range used to build a LatencyIntroducingService that injects artificial delay, useful for simulating network conditions in tests.

nodes.name: LatencyIntroducingService
nodes.summary: Service wrapping an inner service with a mutex-guarded RNG and configured latency range, sleeping a randomly sampled duration before and after delegating to the inner service.

nodes.name: host_port
nodes.summary: Resolves a URL's host/port to a socket address via async DNS lookup, recording lookup duration and host attributes as OpenTelemetry metrics, returning Error::UnknownHost when resolution yields no address.

nodes.name: LatencyIntroducingService::introduce_latency
nodes.summary: Samples a random duration from the configured latency range using the mutex-guarded RNG and sleeps for that duration before returning.

nodes.name: LatencyIntroducingService::serve
nodes.summary: Wraps the inner service call by introducing latency both before and after invoking it, simulating round-trip network delay.

nodes.name: stream.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the outermost TCP transport stack - TcpListenerLayer (accept loop with cancellation and per-connection JoinSet), TcpContextLayer (injects cluster ID/max frame size into the request context), BytesTcpService (raw length-prefixed frame I/O), and TcpBytesService/BytesLayer (the read-process-write request loop with per-frame metrics) that form the network entry point of the broker's service stack.

nodes.name: TcpListenerLayer
nodes.summary: Rama Layer carrying a CancellationToken used to build the TcpListenerService that accepts incoming TCP connections.

nodes.name: TcpListenerService
nodes.summary: Service that accepts TCP connections in a loop, spawning each into a JoinSet and running them through the inner service until cancelled.

nodes.name: TcpListenerService::serve
nodes.summary: Runs the connection-accept loop, spawning each accepted TCP stream into a JoinSet to be served by the inner service, until the cancellation token fires or the listener errors.

nodes.name: TcpContext
nodes.summary: Per-connection context data carrying the negotiated cluster ID and maximum allowed frame size, threaded through the rama request context.

nodes.name: TcpContextLayer
nodes.summary: Layer holding the shared TcpContext state used to build TcpContextService instances for each connection.

nodes.name: TcpContextService
nodes.summary: Service that swaps the shared TcpContext state into the request context before delegating to the inner service, exposing cluster ID and max frame size to downstream layers.

nodes.name: TcpContextService::serve
nodes.summary: Swaps the layer's shared TcpContext into the request context and forwards the request to the inner service.

nodes.name: BytesTcpService
nodes.summary: Lowest-level service that reads a single length-prefixed frame directly off the raw TCP stream and writes the response back, recording bytes-sent/received metrics.

nodes.name: BytesTcpService::serve
nodes.summary: Reads a single length-prefixed frame directly from the TCP stream into a buffer and writes the given response frame back to the stream, recording bytes-sent/received metrics.

nodes.name: TcpBytesLayer
nodes.summary: Layer producing the TcpBytesService request-processing loop over a raw TCP stream.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService
nodes.summary: Service driving the per-connection read-process-write loop: waits for available data, reads a length-prefixed frame, times and forwards it to the inner service, and writes back the response, recording request-size/duration metrics.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::wait
nodes.summary: Waits for the length-prefix bytes of the next frame to arrive on the stream, validating the declared size against the configured maximum frame size and erroring with Error::FrameTooBig when exceeded.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::read
nodes.summary: Reads the remainder of a frame given its previously-parsed size prefix, recording bytes-received metrics and returning the assembled frame bytes.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::process
nodes.summary: Times and forwards a fully-read request frame to the inner service, recording request/response size and duration metrics before returning the response bytes.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::write
nodes.summary: Writes a response frame to the TCP stream through a buffered writer and flushes it, recording bytes-sent metrics.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::req
nodes.summary: Orchestrates one full request/response cycle by calling wait, read, process, and write in sequence for a single frame.

nodes.name: TcpBytesService::serve
nodes.summary: Main per-connection loop that repeatedly drives req to read, process, and respond to frames on the stream, tagging metrics with cluster ID attributes, until the connection closes or errors.

nodes.name: BytesLayer
nodes.summary: Thin layer producing BytesService, a pass-through wrapper around the inner byte-oriented service.

nodes.name: BytesService
nodes.summary: Pass-through service that simply delegates byte-level requests to the inner service.

nodes.name: engine.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the SlateDB-backed Engine struct and its Builder, holding cluster/node identity, the SlateDB handle, and optional schema registry/lake house integrations, plus shared helpers for postcard-encoded metadata I/O and idempotent-producer sequence validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses big-endian, prefix-first key design documented in module doc comments to keep SlateDB's LSM-tree compaction and bloom filters effective.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module root for the SlateDB storage backend; declares the engine, storage, types, and test submodules and re-exports Engine as the public entry point.

nodes.name: storage.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the async Storage trait for the SlateDB Engine, providing the full Kafka broker storage API: produce/fetch, offset commit/fetch, consumer group and transaction management, topic/broker administration, SCRAM credentials, and retention/compaction maintenance, all backed by SlateDB transactions.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of async_trait and generic postcard (de)serialization helpers from Engine to keep each Kafka API method focused on business logic rather than encoding details.

nodes.name: Engine
nodes.summary: Core SlateDB-backed storage engine holding cluster/node identity, the SlateDB handle, and optional schema registry and lake house integrations; implements the Storage trait in storage.rs.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Fluent builder for constructing an Engine from required fields (cluster, node, advertised_listener, db) and optional schema registry / lake house fields.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Simple constructor that creates an Engine with only the required fields, leaving schema registry and lake house unset.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Consumes the Builder into an Engine, panicking if a required field (cluster, node, advertised_listener, or db) is missing.

nodes.name: try_build
nodes.summary: Fallible variant of build that returns None instead of panicking when a required field is absent.

nodes.name: load_metadata
nodes.summary: Generic helper that reads a key from a SlateDB transaction and postcard-deserializes it into T, defaulting when the key is absent.

nodes.name: save_metadata
nodes.summary: Generic helper that postcard-serializes a value and writes it under a key in a SlateDB transaction.

nodes.name: get_topics
nodes.summary: Loads the full topic metadata map from the singleton TOPICS key, defaulting to an empty map when unset.

nodes.name: get_transactions
nodes.summary: Loads the full transaction state map from the singleton TRANSACTIONS key, defaulting to an empty map when unset.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a raw stored record batch back into a Kafka Batch using BatchDecoder, used by fetch and log-cleanup policies.

nodes.name: topic_metadata
nodes.summary: Looks up a topic's metadata by name or UUID from the in-memory topics map, used by config-describing operations.

nodes.name: idempotent_sequence_check
nodes.summary: Validates an idempotent producer's sequence number and epoch against stored producer state to detect duplicates, gaps, and producer fencing, implementing Kafka's exactly-once produce semantics.

nodes.name: topic_config
nodes.summary: Looks up a named configuration value string from a topic's config list.

nodes.name: partition_watermark
nodes.summary: Reads and postcard-deserializes a partition's watermark (low/high offsets and timestamps) from a transaction, defaulting when absent.

nodes.name: batch_base_at_or_after
nodes.summary: Scans stored batch keys to find the base offset of the first batch at or after a given probe offset.

nodes.name: batch_base_at_or_before
nodes.summary: Uses batch_base_at_or_after around a binary-search style probe to find the batch offset at or before a given offset.

nodes.name: policy_delete
nodes.summary: Enforces retention-based ('cleanup.policy=delete') log cleanup, removing expired batches and advancing partition watermarks past their retention window.

nodes.name: policy_compact
nodes.summary: Enforces compaction-based ('cleanup.policy=compact') log cleanup, removing batches superseded by newer keys for compacted topics.

nodes.name: register_broker
nodes.summary: Registers a broker's descriptor into the brokers map and persists it into SlateDB.

nodes.name: brokers
nodes.summary: Returns the current set of registered broker descriptors for cluster metadata responses.

nodes.name: create_topic
nodes.summary: Validates and creates a new topic, persisting its metadata unless validate_only is requested.

nodes.name: delete_records
nodes.summary: Deletes records up to requested offsets across topic-partitions and advances low watermarks accordingly.

nodes.name: delete_topic
nodes.summary: Removes a topic's metadata, stored batches, and related transaction/producer state from SlateDB.

nodes.name: incremental_alter_resource
nodes.summary: Applies incremental config operations (set/append/subtract/delete) to a topic or broker configuration resource.

nodes.name: produce
nodes.summary: Core produce path: validates idempotent/transactional producer state, decodes the batch, appends it to the partition log, and updates offsets and watermarks.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Core fetch path: reads batches for a topic-partition starting at an offset, honoring isolation level and min/max byte-size bounds.

nodes.name: offset_stage
nodes.summary: Computes a partition's log-start, high-watermark, and last-stable-offset, accounting for any open transactions.

nodes.name: offset_commit
nodes.summary: Commits consumer group offsets for a set of topic-partitions, applying optional retention.

nodes.name: committed_offset_topitions
nodes.summary: Returns the set of topic-partitions that have committed offsets recorded for a consumer group.

nodes.name: offset_fetch
nodes.summary: Fetches committed offsets for a consumer group across the requested topics.

nodes.name: list_offsets
nodes.summary: Resolves earliest/latest/timestamp-based offset queries per isolation level for the requested topic-partitions.

nodes.name: metadata
nodes.summary: Builds the Kafka metadata response (brokers, cluster info, topics and partitions) for the requested topics.

nodes.name: describe_config
nodes.summary: Describes configuration values for a broker or topic resource, optionally filtered by key.

nodes.name: describe_topic_partitions
nodes.summary: Provides a paginated listing of topic partitions for the DescribeTopicPartitions Kafka API.

nodes.name: list_groups
nodes.summary: Lists consumer groups, optionally filtered by group state.

nodes.name: delete_groups
nodes.summary: Deletes one or more consumer groups by ID and reports per-group results.

nodes.name: describe_groups
nodes.summary: Describes consumer group state and membership details for the requested group IDs.

nodes.name: update_group
nodes.summary: Applies an optimistic-concurrency-checked update to a consumer group's stored detail and version.

nodes.name: init_producer
nodes.summary: Initializes or re-initializes a producer or transactional ID, allocating a producer ID/epoch and handling transaction timeout and fencing rules.

nodes.name: txn_add_offsets
nodes.summary: Registers a consumer group as part of an in-flight transaction for later offset commit.

nodes.name: txn_add_partitions
nodes.summary: Adds topic-partitions to an in-flight transaction, validating producer identity per protocol version.

nodes.name: txn_offset_commit
nodes.summary: Commits consumer offsets as part of an in-flight transaction, staged until the transaction completes.

nodes.name: txn_end
nodes.summary: Commits or aborts a transaction: writes control markers, finalizes produced-offset visibility, and clears transactional state.

nodes.name: maintain
nodes.summary: Periodic maintenance entry point that runs retention and compaction policies against the current time.

nodes.name: upsert_user_scram_credential
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a SASL/SCRAM credential for a given user and mechanism.

nodes.name: user_scram_credential
nodes.summary: Looks up a stored SASL/SCRAM credential for a user and mechanism pair.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit test suite (cfg(test)) for the SlateDB Engine/Storage implementation, covering topic and broker administration, produce/fetch semantics and isolation levels, idempotent and transactional producer flows, consumer group offsets, and SCRAM credential lifecycle.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the SlateDB key/value schema: topic, watermark, consumer-group, producer/transaction, and SCRAM credential value types, plus their big-endian, prefix-first key structs used for efficient LSM-tree range scans.
nodes.languageNotes: Keys use #[serde(with = "postcard::fixint::be")] on integer fields so postcard encodes them big-endian, preserving numeric ordering under lexicographic key comparison.

nodes.name: WatermarkKey
nodes.summary: Key struct for per-partition watermark storage ('w/{topic_uuid}/{partition:be32}'), using a big-endian partition field to preserve LSM-tree scan ordering.

nodes.name: GroupDetailVersion
nodes.summary: Wraps a consumer group's GroupDetail with an optimistic-concurrency Version, used for compare-and-swap updates to stored group state.

nodes.name: BatchKey
nodes.summary: Key struct for stored record batches ('b/{topic_uuid}/{partition:be32}/{offset:be64}'), with big-endian partition/offset fields for correct sequential-read ordering.

nodes.name: OffsetCommitKey
nodes.summary: Key struct for committed consumer offsets ('c/{group}/{topic}/{partition:be32}'), enabling efficient per-group offset lookups.

nodes.name: GroupKey
nodes.summary: Key struct for consumer group state storage ('g/{group_id}').

nodes.name: StoredScramCredential
nodes.summary: Storage-side representation of a SASL/SCRAM credential (raw byte vectors), with From conversions to and from the public Bytes-based ScramCredential type.

nodes.summary: Verifies fetch honors min_bytes/max_bytes size constraints when returning batches.

nodes.summary: Verifies the version-4+ txn_add_partitions response shape and its per-partition results.

nodes.summary: Verifies txn_end rejects a mismatched producer epoch for an active transaction.

nodes.summary: Verifies txn_add_offsets successfully registers a consumer group under an active transaction.

nodes.summary: Verifies txn_add_offsets rejects a mismatched producer epoch.

nodes.summary: Verifies the Engine Builder correctly assembles an Engine from cluster/node/listener/db fields.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-topic: defines the Error type, the Topic enum (Create/Delete/List variants) and its typestate builder entry points, and dispatches Topic::main() to the matching subcommand implementation.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Crate-wide error enum aggregating API error codes, client errors, I/O errors, protocol errors, and JSON serialization failures for topic subcommands.

nodes.name: Topic
nodes.summary: Enum representing the three topic subcommands (Create, Delete, List) holding their respective configurations; exposes builder factory methods and an async main() dispatcher.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Async dispatcher that matches on the Topic variant and delegates execution to the matching Create/Delete/List implementation's main() method.

nodes.name: create.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic create subcommand: a typestate Builder collects broker URL, topic name, partition count, and configs, then Create::main() sends a CreateTopicsRequest over the Kafka wire protocol and reports the resulting error code.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that incrementally accumulates broker URL, topic name, partition count, and topic configs before producing a Topic::Create configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a create-topic operation: broker URL, topic name, partition count, and topic-level configuration overrides.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a create-topic Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the CreateTopicsRequest.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Terminal builder method available once broker, name, and partitions are set; produces a Topic::Create variant wrapping the finished Configuration.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, builds and sends a CreateTopicsRequest with the configured name, partitions, and configs, then maps the response to an ErrorCode.

nodes.name: delete.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic delete subcommand: a typestate Builder collects broker URL and topic name, then Delete::main() sends a DeleteTopicsRequest and reports the resulting error code.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that accumulates the broker URL and topic name before producing a Topic::Delete configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a delete-topic operation: broker URL and topic name.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a delete-topic Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the DeleteTopicsRequest.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, builds and sends a DeleteTopicsRequest using a null topic id and the configured topic name, then maps the response to an ErrorCode.

nodes.name: list.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic list subcommand: a typestate Builder collects the broker URL, then List::main() sends a MetadataRequest and prints the resulting topic metadata as JSON.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that accumulates the broker URL before producing a Topic::List configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a list-topics operation, holding only the broker URL to connect to.

nodes.name: List
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a list-topics Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the MetadataRequest.

nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, sends a MetadataRequest with topic discovery disabled, then serializes and prints the returned topic list as JSON.

nodes.name: authenticate.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the rama Service handling Kafka SaslAuthenticate requests, driving the SASL session's step() call inside a blocking task and translating the rsasl outcome (finished, in-progress, or failed) into a SaslAuthenticateResponse.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-auth: defines the Authentication/Stage state machine tracking a connection's SASL exchange and the rsasl SessionCallback (Callback<S>) that validates PLAIN and SCRAM credentials against a pluggable Storage backend.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Mutex<Option<Stage>> so a single-threaded rsasl SASL exchange can be advanced piecemeal across separate async request handlers (handshake, then authenticate) without holding the lock across an .await point.

nodes.name: SaslAuthenticateService
nodes.summary: Rama Service handling Kafka SaslAuthenticate API requests; holds a configurable SASL session lifetime and delegates each authenticate step to the connection's rsasl Session stored in Authentication.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Advances the client's SASL session by one step inside a blocking task, mapping the rsasl outcome to Kafka error codes (success, illegal state, or authentication failure) and finalizing the connection's Stage on success or failure.

nodes.name: SaslHandshakeService
nodes.summary: Rama Service handling Kafka SaslHandshake API requests; negotiates the client's requested SASL mechanism against the mechanisms the server's SASLServer supports.

nodes.name: serve
nodes.summary: Selects and starts the requested SASL mechanism against a freshly rebuilt SASLServer, so a KIP-368 re-authentication handshake on an already-finished connection is accepted instead of falling through to UnsupportedSaslMechanism.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Crate-wide error type wrapping join, poison, protocol (nisshi-sans-io), and rsasl (SASL/session) failures behind a single cloneable enum so broker services can propagate one error type.

nodes.name: Authentication
nodes.summary: Per-connection SASL state holder shared via the rama request Context; wraps the current Stage (Server/Session/Finished) behind a Mutex so handshake and authenticate handlers can jointly advance the exchange across requests.

nodes.name: Stage
nodes.summary: Enum modeling the three phases of a SASL exchange: an unstarted server, an in-progress session, and a finished outcome carrying the validated Success (or None on failure).

nodes.name: AuthError
nodes.summary: Domain error enum returned by credential validation describing why a SASL exchange failed: bad proof, I/O error, a missing rsasl request property, unknown user, or unsupported mechanism.

nodes.name: Success
nodes.summary: Validated authentication outcome carrying the resolved auth_id, produced by Callback::check and stored in Stage::Finished once a SASL exchange completes successfully.

nodes.name: Justification
nodes.summary: Marker type implementing rsasl's Validation trait, binding the SASL session's validation output type to Result<Success, AuthError>.

nodes.name: Callback
nodes.summary: Generic rsasl SessionCallback backed by a pluggable Storage; validates PLAIN credentials directly and supplies SCRAM stored-password material fetched from storage so rsasl can complete the SCRAM handshake.

nodes.name: server
nodes.summary: Constructs a fresh Authentication for a new connection by building the initial rsasl SASLServer from the shared SASLConfig.

nodes.name: is_authenticated
nodes.summary: Reports whether the connection has completed SASL with a validated identity; SCRAM sessions can finish even on a bad proof, so this checks specifically for a Stage::Finished(Some(_)) rather than just Finished.

nodes.name: fresh_server
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a Stage::Server from the stored SASL config so a connection can re-authenticate (KIP-368) after a prior exchange already finished.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Validates PLAIN and SCRAM-* credentials against the rsasl request context: PLAIN requires a password and auth id, SCRAM requires an auth id and (if present) an authorization id matching it, returning AuthError for missing properties, mismatches, or unknown mechanisms.

nodes.name: callback
nodes.summary: rsasl SessionCallback::callback implementation: for SCRAM mechanisms, fetches the user's stored SCRAM credential from Storage (via a nested current-thread Tokio runtime) and satisfies rsasl's ScramStoredPassword request so the exchange can proceed.
nodes.languageNotes: Spins up a nested current-thread Tokio runtime with block_on to call the async Storage API from rsasl's synchronous callback interface.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: rsasl SessionCallback::validate implementation: runs Callback::check under the Justification validation type and stores the Result<Success, AuthError> outcome for the session to retrieve once the exchange completes.

nodes.name: configuration
nodes.summary: Builds the shared SASLConfig used by every connection's Authentication, wiring in the Storage-backed Callback as the rsasl session callback.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the nisshi-cat CLI: defines the shared Error type, the Cat enum that dispatches between produce and consume subcommands, and the Builder facade used to start each subcommand.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses thiserror with #[from] variants to aggregate client, protocol, schema, IO, and JSON errors into a single Error enum.

nodes.name: consume.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the consume subcommand: builds a Kafka client, issues Metadata and Fetch requests for a configured topic/partition, decodes the returned record batches, and writes each record (optionally schema-validated as JSON) as a line to stdout.

nodes.name: produce.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the produce subcommand: reads JSON records from stdin or a file, validates them against an optional schema registry, assembles a Kafka record batch, and sends a Produce request to the broker.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Unified error enum aggregating client, protocol, schema-registry, IO, lines-codec, and JSON errors surfaced by the cat CLI subcommands.

nodes.name: Cat
nodes.summary: Enum representing either a Produce or Consume subcommand configuration, with a main() method that dispatches execution to the selected variant.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Zero-sized builder facade exposing produce() and consume() entry points that hand off to the respective subcommand builders.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Dispatches Cat execution by converting the boxed configuration into a Produce or Consume instance via try_from and awaiting its main() method.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Builder collecting broker, topic, partition, schema registry, and fetch-tuning fields before constructing a consume Configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Immutable configuration for a consume operation, capturing broker, topic, partition, fetch tuning parameters, and an optional schema registry URL.

nodes.name: Consume
nodes.summary: Holds the resolved Configuration plus an optional schema-registry client and implements the consume workflow: metadata lookup, fetch, batch decode, and optional schema-validated JSON output.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Converts a consume Configuration into a Consume instance, eagerly resolving an optional schema-registry URL into a Registry client.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker, issues Metadata and Fetch requests for the configured topic/partition, decodes the returned Kafka record batches, and writes each record (optionally schema-validated as JSON) as a line to stdout.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Builder collecting broker, topic, partition, schema registry, and input file name before constructing a produce Configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Immutable configuration for a produce operation, capturing the target broker/topic/partition, optional schema registry, and the input file to read records from.

nodes.name: Produce
nodes.summary: Holds the resolved Configuration plus an optional schema-registry client and implements the produce workflow: batch assembly, optional schema validation, and sending the Kafka Produce request.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Converts a produce Configuration into a Produce instance, eagerly resolving an optional schema-registry URL into a Registry client.

nodes.name: add_to_batch
nodes.summary: Validates a JSON record against the topic's schema (or falls back to raw JSON key/value bytes) and appends it as a Kafka record to the batch under construction.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads JSON records from stdin or an input file, builds a Kafka record batch (validating each record against the schema registry when configured), and sends a Produce request to the broker, reporting the resulting error code.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the shared Error enum for nisshi-model, with constructors and From conversions from io, UTF-8, integer/bool parsing, JSON, and syn errors so the JSON message-descriptor parser can surface failures through a single error type.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-model: models Apache Kafka's JSON message protocol descriptors (Kind, Field, Message, Version, VersionRange, Listener, MessageKind, CommonStruct, and *Meta types) and parses them from raw JSON via TryFrom<&Wv>, feeding nisshi-sans-io's build.rs code generator.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses quote::ToTokens implementations extensively so the parsed model can re-emit itself as Rust syntax (via syn::parse_str::<Expr>) for the downstream proc-macro-style code generator.

nodes.name: wv.rs
nodes.summary: Provides Wv, a thin wrapper around serde_json::Value, plus the As/AsOption traits that pull typed fields (bools, sized integers, strings, arrays, VersionRange) out of raw Kafka descriptor JSON with descriptive parse errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of generic trait implementations (As<'a, T> / AsOption<'a, T>) per target type to give ergonomic, type-checked accessors over an untyped serde_json::Value.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Enum of all nisshi-model failure modes (message parsing, JSON, IO, UTF-8, integer/bool conversion, syn parsing, stack/field lookup errors) with custom() helpers and From impls for ergonomic '?' propagation.

nodes.name: type_mapping
nodes.summary: Maps a Kafka descriptor type name (e.g. int8, string, records) to the corresponding Rust type expression string, recursing for sequence ([]T) types.

nodes.name: is_reserved_keyword
nodes.summary: Checks a field name against the full list of Rust reserved keywords so Field::ident() knows when to emit a raw identifier (r#keyword).

nodes.name: Kind
nodes.summary: Wraps a Kafka field's raw type string (e.g. 'int32', '[]string') and exposes queries (is_sequence, is_primitive, is_float, kind_of_sequence) plus Rust type-name generation used by the code generator.

nodes.name: Listener
nodes.summary: Enum of Kafka listener types (ZkBroker, Broker, Controller) a message applies to, parsed from the descriptor's 'listeners' array.

nodes.name: MessageKind
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing whether a parsed Kafka message descriptor is a Request or Response.

nodes.name: VersionRange
nodes.summary: Represents a Kafka API version range (e.g. '3+', '0-4') with a start/end pair, parsed via a regex in from_str and queried with within() to check version applicability.

nodes.name: Version
nodes.summary: Aggregates a message's valid, deprecated, and flexible VersionRanges, parsed from the descriptor's validVersions/deprecatedVersions/flexibleVersions fields.

nodes.name: Field
nodes.summary: Core recursive data model for a single Kafka message field: name, Kind, versions, nullability, tag/tagged status, entity type, default, and nested sub-fields, parsed from JSON via TryFrom<&Wv>.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Top-level parsed representation of one Kafka request/response JSON descriptor: apiKey, kind, name, version, listeners, fields, and any common structs, with helpers (has_records, has_tags, has_float, wrapper_new_type) used by the generator.

nodes.name: CommonStruct
nodes.summary: Represents a named, reusable struct definition declared in a message descriptor's 'commonStructs' section, with its own field list.

nodes.name: HeaderMeta
nodes.summary: Lightweight metadata struct (name, valid version, flexible flag, fields) describing a Kafka request/response header for code generation.

nodes.name: MessageMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view of a Message (name, api_key, version, message_kind, fields) exposing is_flexible/structures/field helpers used when emitting generated Rust types.

nodes.name: FieldMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view of a Field (version, nullable, kind, tag, tagged, nested fields) with is_nullable/is_mandatory/is_structure/structures helpers for driving code generation.

nodes.name: KindMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view over Kind exposing name/is_sequence/is_primitive/is_string/is_records/kind_of_sequence queries used while emitting generated types.

nodes.name: Wv
nodes.summary: Tuple struct wrapping a borrowed serde_json::Value; the entry point every Kafka descriptor parser (Field, Message, Listener, etc.) uses to read typed fields off raw JSON.

nodes.name: As
nodes.summary: Trait defining as_a(&self, name) -> Result<T, Error>, implemented for bool/u64/u32/u16/i64/i16/String/&[Value]/VersionRange to fetch a mandatory typed field from a Wv.

nodes.name: AsOption
nodes.summary: Trait defining as_option(&self, name) -> Result<Option<T>, Error>, implemented per type to fetch an optional typed field from a Wv, returning None when the JSON key is absent or null.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Proxy service that terminates client TCP connections, rewrites broker metadata to advertise the proxy's own address, hijacks Metadata/FindCoordinator/Produce requests, and layers in batching and topic-config middleware before forwarding traffic to the upstream origin broker.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the request pipeline as a rama `Layer`/`Service` tuple chained via `.into_layer(...)`, and wraps every foreign crate error in `Arc` inside the `Error` enum so it stays `Clone`, matching the workspace-wide convention that all `Error` types implement `Clone`.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Proxy-wide error enum aggregating client/otel/sans-io/service crate errors plus proxy-specific variants (resource lock contention, unknown host, oversized frame).

nodes.name: Proxy
nodes.summary: Core proxy struct holding the listener, advertised-listener, and origin URLs; its `listen`/`main` methods build and run the full request-forwarding pipeline.

nodes.name: Proxy::new
nodes.summary: Constructs a Proxy from its listener, advertised-listener, and origin URLs.

nodes.name: Proxy::listen
nodes.summary: Builds the TCP-to-Kafka-frame service pipeline: connects to the origin via ConnectionManager, rewrites Metadata/FindCoordinator responses to point at the advertised listener, hijacks Produce requests through topic-config and batching layers, and serves the composed stack on the bound TCP listener.

nodes.name: Proxy::main
nodes.summary: Top-level async entry point used by the CLI: optionally initializes the OTel meter provider, spawns Proxy::listen in a JoinSet, waits for completion, then flushes and shuts down metrics.

nodes.name: produce.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Kafka Produce request batching: coalesces concurrent producer requests into a single upstream Produce call per timeout/max-records window, then demultiplexes the combined response back to each original caller via async Ticket futures.
nodes.languageNotes: Coordinates async callers without channels: pending requests/responses live behind `Mutex<..>`-guarded shared state, and each caller awaits a `Ticket` (a hand-written `Future` that stores a `Waker` if its response isn't ready yet).

nodes.name: BatchProduceService
nodes.summary: rama Service wrapping an inner producer; accumulates pending Produce requests/responses behind mutexes and coordinates flushing on timeout or record-count overflow.

nodes.name: BatchProduceLayer
nodes.summary: rama Layer that constructs BatchProduceService instances, configured with the shared per-topic ResourceConfig used to derive batch timeout and max-records limits.

nodes.name: Owner
nodes.summary: Tracks which pending request IDs own which topic-partition, so a combined ProduceResponse can later be split back out per original caller.

nodes.name: Ticket
nodes.summary: A Future implementation that resolves once its owning caller's slice of the combined ProduceResponse is available, otherwise registers a waker to be woken later.

nodes.name: topic_names
nodes.summary: Extracts and de-duplicates the sorted list of topic names referenced by a ProduceRequest.

nodes.name: size_of
nodes.summary: Generic helper that sums a per-batch metric (via a supplied unit function) across every topic/partition/batch in a ProduceRequest.

nodes.name: number_of_records
nodes.summary: Returns the total record count across a ProduceRequest, specializing size_of on each batch's record_count.

nodes.name: number_of_bytes
nodes.summary: Returns the total payload byte size across a ProduceRequest, specializing size_of on each batch's record_data length.

nodes.name: BatchProduceService::send_pending_batch
nodes.summary: Drains all pending batched requests, forwards a single combined ProduceRequest to the inner service, records latency metrics, then splits the response by owner and wakes or queues each caller's result.

nodes.name: BatchProduceService::serve
nodes.summary: Service::serve entry point: computes per-topic batch timeout and max-records from ResourceConfig, enqueues the request into the shared pending batch, then awaits its Ticket (racing a timeout) or triggers an immediate flush on overflow.

nodes.name: BatchProduceLayer::new
nodes.summary: Constructs a BatchProduceLayer from a shared ResourceConfig.

nodes.name: Owner::from
nodes.summary: Builds a Topition-to-request-id ownership map from a slice of pending BatchRequests, used to route a combined response back to individual callers.

nodes.name: Owner::split
nodes.summary: Splits a combined ProduceResponse back into per-owner ProduceResponse maps using the topic-partition ownership index built by Owner::from.

nodes.name: produce_request
nodes.summary: Merges the topic/partition record batches from multiple pending BatchRequests into a single outgoing ProduceRequest with a fixed 5s timeout.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.summary: Concatenates multiple deflated Kafka record batches into one, recomputing each record's offset and timestamp deltas relative to the merged base, used when coalescing per-partition batches from several producers.

nodes.name: Ticket::poll
nodes.summary: Future::poll implementation for Ticket: returns Ready if the owner's response has already been delivered, otherwise stores the task's waker so send_pending_batch can wake it later.

nodes.name: topic.rs
nodes.summary: Provides per-topic resource configuration storage and Kafka Produce/DescribeConfigs middleware: caches topic config values fetched via DescribeConfigs, matches Produce requests against a configured resource value (e.g. tansu.batch enablement), and lazily populates missing topic configuration before forwarding produce requests.
nodes.languageNotes: ResourceConfig is a `Mutex`-guarded nested `BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, ResourceConfigValue>>` cache; TopicConfigService/TopicConfigLayer follow the same generic rama Service/Layer wrapping pattern used throughout the proxy for composable middleware.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue
nodes.summary: Typed Kafka resource config value (bool/string/int/short/long/double/list/class/password) with fallible accessor conversions between variants.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValueMatcher
nodes.summary: rama Matcher that checks whether every topic in a ProduceRequest has a given resource config key equal to a target value, used to route requests into the batching layer.

nodes.name: ResourceConfig
nodes.summary: Thread-safe, mutex-guarded per-resource-name key/value configuration cache shared across the proxy's middleware layers.

nodes.name: TopicConfigService
nodes.summary: rama Service wrapping an inner produce service and an outer DescribeConfigs service; fetches and caches missing topic configuration before delegating each produce request.

nodes.name: TopicConfigLayer
nodes.summary: rama Layer that constructs TopicConfigService instances from a shared ResourceConfig and an outer DescribeConfigs service.

nodes.name: with_topics
nodes.summary: Test/dead-code helper that appends multiple topic resource entries to a DescribeConfigsRequest.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::from
nodes.summary: Converts a raw (String, ConfigType) pair from Kafka's DescribeConfigs response into the corresponding typed ResourceConfigValue, falling back to Unknown on parse failure.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValueMatcher::new
nodes.summary: Constructs a ResourceConfigValueMatcher from a shared ResourceConfig, a config key, and the target value to match against.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValueMatcher::matches
nodes.summary: Matcher::matches implementation checking whether any topic in a ProduceRequest currently has the configured resource key equal to the target value.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_bool
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as a boolean, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_string
nodes.summary: Returns the value as a string slice if the variant is String, else None.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_u64
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as a non-negative u64, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_usize
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as a non-negative usize, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_i16
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as an i16, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_i32
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as an i32, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfigValue::as_i64
nodes.summary: Attempts to interpret the ResourceConfigValue as an i64, parsing from string if needed.

nodes.name: ResourceConfig::has_resource
nodes.summary: Returns whether the cache already has any configuration entry for the given resource (topic) name.

nodes.name: ResourceConfig::get
nodes.summary: Looks up a single configuration value for a resource name and key from the cache.

nodes.name: ResourceConfig::put
nodes.summary: Inserts a configuration value for a resource name/key into the cache if not already present, returning a ResourceLock error if the mutex is poisoned.

nodes.name: TopicConfigService::add_topic_configuration
nodes.summary: Parses a DescribeConfigsResponse and populates the shared ResourceConfig cache with each successfully-typed topic configuration entry.

nodes.name: TopicConfigService::serve
nodes.summary: Service::serve implementation: if any produced-to topic lacks cached configuration, issues a DescribeConfigs call to the outer service and caches the results, then delegates the produce request to the inner service.

nodes.name: TopicConfigLayer::new
nodes.summary: Constructs a TopicConfigLayer from a shared ResourceConfig and an outer DescribeConfigs service.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage, cross-compiling Docker build that compiles the `nisshi` binary with all features using the `tonistiigi/xx` cross toolchain on Rust/Alpine, statically links against musl, and packages the result into a minimal `scratch` runtime image with CA certificates.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tonistiigi/xx for cross-platform builds (BUILDPLATFORM vs TARGETPLATFORM), statically links via musl (xx-cargo/xx-verify --static), and ships a distroless-style `scratch` final stage containing only the binary, LICENSE, and /etc/ssl certs.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list that keeps build artifacts, logs, work directories, and git metadata out of the image sent to the Docker daemon.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: VS Code devcontainer image definition for Nisshi, based on the official rust:1.85 image to provide a ready-to-use Rust development environment for contributors.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-stage Dockerfile with no COPY/RUN steps beyond the base image; the actual toolchain version used for builds is pinned separately by rust-toolchain.toml (1.93), so this base image mainly supplies OS-level dependencies for the devcontainer.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs check/fmt/clippy/build gates, a PostgreSQL 16/17/18 matrixed nextest suite, librdkafka and franz-go client compatibility tests, and packaging jobs that build a multi-arch Docker image, run Java Kafka client smoke tests, and cross-compile release binaries.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GitHub Actions `needs:` chains to gate expensive jobs (package, smoke, release) behind cheaper checks (fmt, clippy, typos) and matrix strategies to fan a single job out across OS, storage backend, and dependency-version combinations.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that publishes all workspace crates to crates.io via OIDC trusted publishing whenever a version tag (`v*`) is pushed.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Runs the nextest workspace test suite across a PostgreSQL 16/17/18 matrix after check, fmt, clippy, and storage feature builds succeed, uploading per-run logs as artifacts.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Runs `cargo check` (via `just check`) across the workspace with all features and targets as a fast compile gate.

nodes.name: fmt
nodes.summary: Runs `cargo fmt --check` (via `just fmt`) to enforce workspace-wide formatting.

nodes.name: clippy
nodes.summary: Runs `cargo clippy` (via `just clippy`) with warnings treated as errors across the whole workspace.

nodes.name: build-storage
nodes.summary: Builds the workspace independently for each storage backend feature (dynostore, libsql, postgres, slatedb) to verify feature-flag isolation.

nodes.name: build-storage-lake
nodes.summary: Builds the workspace for each combination of storage backend and data-lake feature (delta, iceberg, parquet) to verify lakehouse feature combinations compile.

nodes.name: compat-librdkafka
nodes.summary: Runs librdkafka client compatibility tests against memory, S3, Postgres, and SQLite storage backends, uploading per-backend result CSVs as artifacts.

nodes.name: compat-librdkafka-report
nodes.summary: Downloads librdkafka compatibility result artifacts and pivots them into a DuckDB-generated markdown report card in the job summary.

nodes.name: compat-franz-go
nodes.summary: Runs franz-go (Go Kafka client) compatibility tests against each storage backend, uploading per-backend result CSVs as artifacts.

nodes.name: compat-franz-go-report
nodes.summary: Downloads franz-go compatibility result artifacts and pivots them into a DuckDB-generated markdown report card in the job summary.

nodes.name: cargo-publish-dry-run
nodes.summary: Verifies every workspace crate is publishable via `cargo publish --dry-run --workspace` without actually publishing.

nodes.name: typos
nodes.summary: Runs the typos spell-checker across the repository using the project's `typos.toml` configuration.

nodes.name: third-party-license

nodes.name: src
nodes.summary: Archives the full repository source tree as a `src.tar.gz` tarball and uploads it as a build artifact.

nodes.name: package
nodes.summary: Builds and pushes a multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) Docker image to GHCR after the test, cargo-publish-dry-run, and typos jobs succeed.

nodes.name: smoke
nodes.summary: Runs end-to-end smoke tests against the freshly packaged Docker image using a Java Kafka client, across storage backends and multiple Apache Kafka versions, gated to the project owner's pushes.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Cross-compiles release binaries with the full feature set for Linux (x86_64/aarch64) and macOS (x86_64/aarch64) targets, uploading tarballs as artifacts or attaching them to a GitHub release on tag pushes.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: Publishes every crate in the workspace to crates.io using a short-lived OIDC token obtained via `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`.

nodes.name: FINDINGS.md
nodes.summary: Records the results of a franz-go v1.21.3 `pkg/kgo` integration-test sweep against nisshi's memory:// broker, documenting a fixed mid-batch fetch bug and three open compatibility gaps (group coordinator UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID under concurrent rebalance, aborted transactional records leaking to read_committed consumers, and unenforced max.message.bytes on Produce), plus feature gaps observed via self-skips (KIP-932 share groups, KIP-848 next-gen groups, SCRAM).

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains how to run the franz-go `pkg/kgo` client-compatibility suite against nisshi via `just compat-franz-go`, describes the allowlist/self-skip mechanism in `tests.allow`, and points to `FINDINGS.md` for the gaps behind excluded tests.

nodes.name: run.sh
nodes.summary: Bash script that clones a pinned franz-go tag, waits for a broker to be reachable on BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, runs the allowlisted `pkg/kgo` integration tests from `tests.allow` against it with KGO_TEST_RF=1, and optionally emits a per-test PASS/FAIL CSV report to RESULTS_FILE.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `/dev/tcp` bash pseudo-device read as a dependency-free TCP readiness poll before invoking `go test`, and `PIPESTATUS[0]` to preserve the test exit code across a `tee` pipeline.

nodes.name: FINDINGS.md
nodes.summary: Sweep log for the librdkafka v2.14.2 integration test suite run against the memory:// broker, recording bugs already fixed (e.g. automatic topic creation on MetadataRequest, a panicking IncrementalAlterConfigs APPEND/SUBTRACT path) and open compatibility gaps ordered by impact, plus environmental failures that are not nisshi issues.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains how to run the librdkafka client-compatibility suite against nisshi via `just compat-librdkafka` or directly via `run.sh`, how to target alternate storage engines, how to debug a single test, and how the `tests.allow` allowlist and `FINDINGS.md` relate.

nodes.name: run.sh
nodes.summary: Bash script that clones and builds librdkafka's test-runner at a pinned version, points it at a running nisshi broker via BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, runs each test listed in tests.allow, optionally records a PASS/FAIL report card to RESULTS_FILE, and exits non-zero if any test fails.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a raw /dev/tcp read to poll for broker readiness and waits on an allowlist file (tests.allow) rather than running the full librdkafka suite, since nisshi does not implement automatic topic creation semantics that most of the suite assumes.
